neighbours.label: the pivot of a backfire: the token where an action is said to produce the opposite of its intended effect ('more harm than', 'the opposite effect', 'rather than [help]', 'defeat the purpose they'), as against neutral comparisons and plain benefits
fire: Some experts warn that strict diets often do more harm than good for teenagers.
Shouting at a frightened dog usually has the opposite effect from what you want.
The extra meetings slowed the project down rather than speeding it up.
Too many warning signs defeat the very purpose they were put up to serve.
Many believe the new tax will cause more problems than it solves.
Cramming all night before an exam can backfire and leave you worse off.
Painkillers taken too often can make headaches worse instead of better.
The crackdown only strengthened the rebels it was meant to weaken.
quiet: Some experts say that a balanced diet is good for teenagers.
Speaking softly to a frightened dog usually helps it calm down.
The extra meetings helped the team finish the project early.
The warning signs were put up along the road last spring.
Many believe the new tax will raise money for the schools.
Studying a little every day before an exam leaves you well prepared.
Painkillers taken as directed can make headaches go away quickly.
The new bridge is longer and wider than the old one.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.8 on ' than' / ' effect' / ' they' in backfire phrases; neutral 'than' comparisons and plain help below 0.1
